author: reek
body: The shapes that make the ARM64 LIR selector build a frame (`codex/plugs/arm64/Arm64Lir.codex`, step 4d). Step 4c emitted straight-line arithmetic with no prologue and no epilogue, so it declined any function whose allocation reached a spill slot or a callee-saved register. These are the functions that reach them.

author: reek
body: Every shape here is order-sensitive. `saved` and `spilled` subtract at each join, so a selector that swapped an ALU operand, loaded a spill slot into the wrong scratch, or restored a callee-saved register over a live value produces a different number rather than the same one. `regs-only` is the control: it fits entirely in registers, takes no frame, and must answer exactly what step 4c already answered for it.

author: reek
body: `unused-first` and `swapped` are the parameter cases. Neither can displace a parameter on this target, and they are here to hold that ground: an unused leading parameter still occupies its own argument register, and a pair read in reverse is a reversed read rather than a reversed allocation. If a future construct ever does displace a parameter, these are the shapes that were already known not to.

author: reek
body: `via-call` calls the framed definitions from a tree-emitted function, so the offsets and arities the selector registers have to be right for an ordinary call to land on a function that moves the stack pointer and puts it back.
